management_steps.details: Immediate severe local pain, generalised paraesthesia/hyperaesthesia, muscle pain and cramps, tremors and fasciculations, involuntary movements, agitation, visual disturbances, hypertension/tachycardia/arrhythmias, general weakness (unable to walk, dysphagia, drooling, difficulty breathing). Severity is usually evident within 15-60 minutes but may be delayed up to 8 hours in adults. In South Africa, severe envenomation (scorpionism) is mainly caused by Parabuthus granulatus and Parabuthus transvaalicus.

Give scorpion antivenom to all patients with symptoms and signs of severe envenomation. Standard dose: 5-10ml IV for both children and adults, diluted in a small volume of normal saline, given over 15 minutes. May take 2-6 hours for maximum effect. An additional 5ml dose may be given after 6 hours if the response to the first dose is inadequate. Observe for 6-12 hours after antivenom administration.

If simple analgesia is ineffective, infiltrate the sting site with local anaesthetic. Opioids are relatively ineffective and increase the risk of respiratory depression. Generalised muscle cramps can be alleviated temporarily (20-30 min) with IV calcium gluconate 10% (adults 10ml, children 0.5ml/kg). Support cardiorespiratory function as needed. Tetanus toxoid if required.

warnings: Do NOT give antihistamines or steroids routinely.

Children may present with a unique form of restlessness (crying and thrashing) indicating severe systemic envenomation — bulbar paralysis with respiratory failure is more frequent in children and is the primary cause of death.
